Volkswagen ID. Tiguan Comes With a Virtual Color Reel to Help US Forget About the Appalling ID.4
20 photos
Photo: AutoYa Interior / YouTube
When the Volkswagen Group introduced the dedicated MEB architecture for electric vehicles, it also established a completely new series of models featuring a common ID. name derivative along with numbers for the namesake Volkswagen brand.
So, we have seen the Volkswagen ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, ID.6, ID.7, or ID.7 Tourer, and so on. The main split faction was the ID. Buzz, which is also spelled differently because there’s a space between ID. and the rest of the name. That’s confusing, right?
Well, we could have gotten accustomed to the confusion if the EVs were better. Luckily, Volkswagen has continuously strived to improve them, and now there’s a new generation of vehicles plus facelifts, like the Volkswagen ID.3 Neo, the ID. Polo and ID. Polo GTI plus ID. Cross, a barrage of models for China, as well as the very important all-new VW ID. Tiguan.
The latter was just revealed as the eagerly awaited Volkswagen ID.4 replacement, a more traditional SUV in terms of design and also featuring an interior brimming with physical controls, just like VW promised. The Volkswagen ID.4 is now retiring, and the ID. Tiguan will replace it along with the ID.5, coming to Europe first but also to the United States ‘at a later date.’
The gasoline, diesel, and hybrid VW Tiguan will continue to exist, and the ID. Tiguan will simply become its EV sibling, with a muscular look and sharp body lines. There are even classic door handles, thank goodness, along with interior physical controls for main functions – AC, the steering wheel, and more. There will be screens, too: a 10-inch digital instrument cluster, a central 15-inch infotainment screen, and also an optional 12-inch passenger screen.
There’s vehicle-to-load functionality, a 1.1 cu. ft. (32-liter) frunk, plus three powertrains: 58 kWh battery with 188 hp and RWD, plus the larger 77-kWh pack with 281 hp and RWD or 295 hp and AWD. What we didn’t get were additional exterior and interior colors: only a black or white option inside and a silver or yellow shade on the outside.
No worries, though, as the good folks over at the "AutoYa" info channel on YouTube have a satellite venue dubbed " AutoYa Interior ," which is where all the CGI VW action resides, and they have a solution. The host of the channel doesn’t need to talk much, as they discuss a model that’s already official. Instead, he gives more time to the resident pixel master to show us the quick comparison to the older VW ID.4.
Afterward, they jump straight into the unofficial, hypothetical color reel, previewing the new model in various color options, like blue, red, green, brown, black, gray, or purple, both inside and outside – as a way to alleviate the fact that an official vehicle configurator tool isn’t available yet. So, what do you think? Do you have a favorite hue already?

Cycliq's Fly12 Sport Is Considered One of the Best Cycling Dashcams out There – Is It GoPro Quality?
13 photos
Photo: Cycliq
As a means of getting from Point A to Point B, cyclists around the world must share the road with cars, motorized beings that protect its occupants with a blend steel, aluminum, and composite carapace, one that often, when clipping a cyclist, isn’t even felt.
In the struggle to make cycling safer for us and even have a clear sight of things after an accident takes place, when recalling details can be a bit fuzzy, Cycliq was born. If you’ve never heard the name, and you ride a bike, it’s time to get with the times because this team has made a name for itself by focusing on developing dash and helmet cams for cyclists .
Photo: Cycliq All of the work they do is in the spirit of reducing hit and run accidents, even ones where the drivers of cars were never aware they caused. Heck, even accidents with other cyclists is one the menu for camera gear of this kind.
All that brings us to the 148-gram trinket, the centerpiece of discussion today. It’s called the Fly12 Sport a $369 piece of equipment from Cycliq that they actually released back in 2022. Keep in mind that Cycliq saw its beginning in 2012, so when they launched the Fly12, the brand declared that it was the culmination of a decade of knowledge and know-how.
Now, the idea behind the Fly12 is very simple, as simple as a dashcam can be. It’s been crafted to record your rides and does so in order to ensure there’s an indisputable image of what happened in case of an accident. But, because it’s designed for bicycles, there are some clear differences between this one and your typical dashboard-mounted options.
Photo: Cycliq For instance, the weight of the system is important in a sector where every gram counts, especially if you’re riding your bike as a means of training, and 148 grams is less than the weight of a GoPro 13. Did I mention that the Fly12 is a two-part system?
Part of the weight of the framework is due to the presence of a 400-lumen headlight that sits side by side the camera, and with four different actions (high and low intensity each), we can tap into lighting solutions for an array of settings, be it cruising the streets or trails, or needing to make your presence known.
Just be sure to keep in mind that using the light will drain the internal 3000 mAh battery, and when coupled with the camera, grants us a runtime of five hours. Thank God its rechargeable. Without the light, we can record for a solid seven hours according to Cycliq. Clearly, adventure cyclists may have trouble keeping this one alive for days.
This brings us to the camera itself, which is showcasing some pretty decent specs in terms of image quality. According to Cycliq’s website, 2560 × 1440p @ 30fps is the peak resolution we can record at, and as an added bonus, we also have the ability to record audio too.
Photo: Cycliq Most importantly though, is the six-axis stabilization that Cycliq has integrated into the Fly12, and if we consider just how bumpy a bicycle ride can be, this feature is essential for catching clear images of license plates that may have caused a spill.
At this stage, I'm thinking that we may just be able to toss this one onto our handlebar and start recording some GoPro-quality videos of our rides. Why not unclip the camera and film your buddies bulling off their stunts? Well, there’s nothing stopping you from doing that, but you will need to color grade those clips if you’re looking to post them to social media.
Also, the wide FOV is bound to affect the shape of objects in the image, and from what I've been noticing in reviews, there doesn’t seem to be a way to modify this distortion in any way. The Fly12 record with 135 degrees FOV.
Photo: Cycliq All the imagery you capture on your rides is stored on a 64 GB microSD card that is included with the system and as it does record, like most other “dashcams,” the Fly12 simply replaces the oldest recordings on the SD card with fresh footage.
Toss in “whatever-proofing,” or IP65-rated, OLED display, and we have ourselves a product that user reviews, all 640 of them, have amassed a 4.6-star rating out of five. That’s quite the rating, and worth considering if you need something like this.
Before I go, allow me to point out that the Fly12 only functions as it faces toward the front of our bikes, and if you want the tap into rear recording, you’ll need to look into another Cycliq product, the Fly6 Pro, this brand’s rear-facing solution. It too, offers a similar runtime, image quality, and FOV. Keep in mind that 270 degrees of coverage does mean that some blind spots exist. Ride safe out there; wear a helmet.

The 2027 Alliance Aurum 38FB Is the Most Beautiful Fifth Wheel RV, Hands Down
38 photos
Photo: Alliance RV
With all the new and innovative releases announced for 2027 from all the major RV players and even some we have never heard of before, it does feel like we're at a turning point in the industry. Alliance RV wants to make sure we know that the surprises are far from over and that they saved the best for last.
They call it the Aurum, the new golden standard in the RV industry and the "new definition of luxury." Aurum is a brand-new, built-from-the-ground-up series of luxury fifth wheels with the Alliance RV badge, designed over the course of two full years and engineered to be different in absolutely every aspect imaginable.
The Alliance Aurum series will include several floorplans , but their exact number or planned release date have not yet been made public. Instead, Alliance is choosing to offer a first taste of it through the introduction of the first completed unit of the Aurum 38FB floorplan, which you can see toured in the video at the bottom of the page. It is, hands down, the most beautiful, elegant, and luxurious fifth wheel RV ever, with the only exception of fully custom rigs.
The Aurum 38FB is a front bathroom floorplan, with a rear living, a middle kitchen, and the bedroom on the upper deck. The layout is common to fifth wheels, but the execution is anything but: Alliance set out to create something different and very sophisticated, and they achieved just that.
Photo: Alliance RV The RV comes in at 41 feet 2 inches (12.5 meters) of length and is built on a 101-inch (256-cm) widebody chassis that Alliance built in-house and named the Fortis. It's engineered to work as one integrated structural system, with 17-inch (43-cm) stacked tube construction and an interlocked Z-beam design, so that it offers more structural strength and better handling, but also a completely unobstructed front basement that's accessible through four different points.
The chassis is a tandem axle dual-wheel one with MORryde independent suspension, hydraulic disc brakes, 17.5-inch H-rated tires, and TPMS. Standard equipment on the outside includes 6-point hydraulic auto-leveling, rear and side camera system with monitor, and a seamless A.R.M.O.R. spray-on roof with one-piece fiberglass caps at the front and rear. The rear one features striking automotive styling.
The sidewalls are 3.5-inch thick, the thickest in the industry . Combined with an upgraded HVAC system, which is also an industry first, and the double-pane argon gas-filled windows, Alliance promises a rolling home – palace, better said – that will remain comfortable throughout the year, fully insulated, and durable.
Photo: Alliance RV While having "only" three slide-outs, the widebody chassis and the smart design allow Alliance to build inside a real home on wheels, of the finest kind. That's not an exaggeration, either: this fifth wheel features stuff you won't find anywhere else, from the GE Cafe appliances (the kind you'll normally find in premium park tiny houses ) to the Italian leather sofa and theater seats, hardwood furniture, and the oversize square windows with built-in sliding blackouts and flyscreens.
As Alliance puts it, this fifth wheel "imagines what a premium fifth wheel can be through thoughtful design, elevated comfort, and an uncompromising approach to the RV experience." Again, not empty words because they're backed by the final product.
This fifth wheel offers sleeping for as many as four people, if you decide to use the living room pull-out sofa as a secondary bedroom. It has two bathrooms, one of which is a half-bath because it doesn't have a shower and the other is a spa-like ensuite complete with a dedicated laundry station (a proper one, not just a washer-dryer closet).
Photo: Alliance RV It has a complete gourmet kitchen where neither functionality nor space is lacking, offering a waterfall island, a full coffee station, a large pantry, and oversize GE appliances, including a dishwasher. It comes with a modular dining space that will adapt to your needs, whether you need a breakfast bar or a dining table for four.
It has a full entertainment lounge with hidden storage behind the entertainment wall and extra nice stuff like hidden cup holders and electric recline function on the premium theater seats.
The Aurum 38FB is specced to be one notch above the rest, with three 15,000-BTU Chill Cube AC units with heat pumps (a fourth is optional), a 40,000-BTU furnace for the house and a separate 25,000-BTU one for the underbelly, a 60,000-BTU on-demand tankless water heater, and 80 lb (36 kg) of propane in total.
Photo: Alliance RV It also comes standard with a Victron energy system with 800W of solar on the roof, a 3000W inverter, and a 400Ah lithium battery. It features ample storage, including a MORryde slide-out tray in that giant basement, several separate exterior bays, an outdoor TV in a dedicated compartment, two Girard legless awnings, and large holding tanks – 98 gallons (371 liters) for freshwater, 106 gallons (401 liters) for gray, and 106 gallons more for black water.
Full automotive bodypaint is included standard, with five options in total to choose from, Tuxedo, Platinum, Executive, Black Label, and Reserve. The unit shown below is in Black Label, a gorgeous, striking matte black that would stand out on its own, even without everything else.
Options include a 60kW NPS generator, a SolarMax+ upgrade on the solar array that will get you full autonomy from the grid, slide toppers, a queen bed instead of the tilting king bed, and a MORryde GooseTech gooseneck box.
Photo: Alliance RV Alliance mentions an empty weight of 20,010 lbs (9,076 kg) and a gross weight of 24,000 lbs (10,886 kg), and a starting MSRP of $269,048. The Aurum 38FB will be produced in just 365 units, and the one below is the first of that series, so that adds to the premium pricing.

Kawasaki Floods the American Market With Tens of Returning Street Motorcycles of All Shapes and Size
6 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
It’s almost mid-October, and this is usually the time when Japanese bike maker Kawasaki launches its fall collection of rides for the coming model year. This time, the collection confirms the return of no less than 20 different two-wheelers, accompanied by their usual variants.
The bikes confirmed to return for the coming model year play in no less than six segments, namely sport, supersport, naked, retro, cruiser, and touring. In all fairness, all these 20 motorcycles don’t bring along any upgrades in terms of fittings, although one can see the availability of new color choices and slightly adjusted price tags.
Taking center stage are the motorcycles playing in the Sport, Supersport, and Hypersport categories. That means the Ninja 500 , Ninja 300, Ninja ZX-4R, Ninja ZX-10R, and Ninja H2, with their respective submodels.
The Ninja 500 bikes (ABS and SE ABS) continue to be powered by the same 451cc parallel-twin engine as before, and will sell starting in late October complete with a full-color TFT instrument panel and a radiator screen, among others. The color choices for the new model year are the same as before.
The smaller Ninja 300 ABS returns as well, packing the standard 296cc liquid-cooled parallel-twin engine tied to an assist and slipper clutch. The bike is fitted with a 37mm telescopic front fork and Uni-Trak rear suspension, and will be available at the end of the month in two color choices.
Photo: Kawasaki The Supersport Ninja ZX-4R ABS and its 4RR offshoot will sell on the American market from late October, with the standard 399cc in-line four-cylinder sitting inside the trellis frame and a Showa suspension system.
Also playing the Supersport game are the Ninja ZX-10R and 10R ABS, powered by a 998cc in-line four-cylinder engine that has defined them for years. The bikes pair that with hardware like Bridgestone Battlax tires pulled over the wheels and Showa suspension hardware.
The Hypersport Kawasaki motorcycles are represented in this release by the Ninja H2 SX SE ABS, which lands with a 998cc in-line four-cylinder engine in the frame, an electronic suspension system, and a 6.5-inch TFT color instrument panel.
For fans of touring bikes, whether we’re talking about sport touring or adventure touring motorcycles, the Japanese bike maker is bringing back the 1100SX ABS, the Versys 650 LT ABS, and the Versys 1100 SE LT ABS. The 1100s are powered by a 1,099cc four-stroke in-line four-cylinder engine, while the smaller Versys carries a fuel-injected 649cc parallel-twin.
Two retro sport motorcycles are next, namely the Z650RS ABS and Z900RS ABS (with SE and Cafe variants in tow), which are also included in the model lineup for next year, packing a 649cc parallel-twin and 948cc in-line four-cylinder engines in their frames, respectively.
Photo: Kawasaki In the naked segment, Kawasaki floods the market for the next few months with the Z500, Z650, Z900, Z125 Pro, and Z H2 SE ABS. As with all the two motorcycles mentioned above, there are no changes to speak of as well.
A trio of motorcycles is thrown into the mix by the Japanese for next year’s retro classic segment, meaning the W175 LTD, W230 ABS, and W800 ABS, powered by engines ranging in displacement from 177cc to 773cc, the same as before.
Last but not least, Kawasaki is bringing back two Vulcans and one Eliminator in the cruiser segment, they too in pretty much the same configuration as before: the Vulcan S with a 649cc engine, the Vulcan 900 with its 903cc powerplant, and the Eliminator 500 packing the 451cc parallel twin in its frame.
All the bikes listed here come, as said, with little to no changes compared to their previous incarnations, but with minor price adjustments. Later in the day, autoevolution will also go through the Kawasaki models that pack a lot more changes.
In the meantime, below this text there is a loong, loong list of prices Kawasaki settled upon for the new model year of its street motorcycles.

DeLorean Goes Flying for Real, Enters Airspeeder International Series as a Constructor
8 photos
Photo: DeLorean
When it comes to carmakers, they don’t get a lot more iconic than DeLorean, even though the brand was never commercially successful. Still, to have them enter a sky-bound racing series as a constructor is a pretty big deal. Meet the DeLorean Airspeeder Team that will take to the skies this November!
DeLorean joins a motorsport built on electric propulsion, advanced flight controls and AI-enabled safety systems. I think Doc Brown would be proud.
Speaking of being proud, DeLorean Motor Company is officially the first-ever American constructor in flying car racing, which is worth certain considerations. It’s not Ford or GM, but a brand that’s been associated with flying since the 80s – albeit only in pop culture.
Meanwhile, the final aircraft design, pilot line-up and full schedule will be revealed soon, ahead of the season opener. And yes, where they're going, they won't need roads. Just had to say it.
“DeLorean has always stood for the courage to imagine transportation differently,” stated company exec, Cameron Wynne. “People have pictured a DeLorean in the sky for forty years. We decided it was time to stop picturing it.”
Meanwhile, Airspeeder founder and CEO, Matt Pearson, had this to say: “DeLorean is the original flying car brand. Long before anyone had built one, the whole world already knew what a flying DeLorean looked like.”
"Every great racing series is defined by the constructors who choose to compete in it. To have an American icon line up on our grid in our first international season tells you where this sport is going. America has repeatedly changed how the world moves, on the road, in the air and beyond, and the DeLorean Airspeeder Team carries that ambition into a new arena.”
How does this work? In the Airspeeder International Series, constructors get to race electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft in three dimensions through electronically defined courses, as opposed to a conventional circuit.
Photo: DeLorean For its debut season, DeLorean will race the Airspeeder Mk3C, but for the 2027-28 season, the company will design a new aircraft in collaboration with student engineering teams at universities across the United States – including the University of California, collaborators at UC Berkeley and Georgia Tech.
As far as I’m concerned, this is way more than just a PR stunt. This is a genuine racing program with actual pilots. However, it remains to be seen how far air mobility can progress in the coming decades outside of special racing events such as this one. I still don’t think we’ll be seeing anything resembling Doc Brown’s flying DeLorean any time soon, if ever.
Is it impossible? No. Just highly improbable. At least for this century. In order to get "there", you'd need a completely revamped infrastructure, fully autonomous eVTOLs , and a complete shift in public perception about cars in general.

2027 Kawasaki Ninja 650 ABS Sportbike Adds Upgraded Suspension and Brakes
14 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
This week marked the start of an invasion of motorcycles made by Japanese Kawasaki. In a single move, the bike maker announced that some 33 two-wheelers are returning for the new model year with minor changes compared to their previous incarnations and slight price adjustments. At the same time, though, four others are coming back with many new things in the bag.
One of the machines that got a significant revamp this week is the Ninja 650 ABS middleweight sportbike. While still retaining the same trellis frame and 649cc parallel-twin engine working a six-speed transmission as before, it now throws in an upgraded suspension system, tweaked brakes, a new instrument display layout, and, for the first time, a very handy option.
The suspension setup changes are, perhaps, the most extensive. Kawasaki opted to go for a new Showa 37mm SFF-BP inverted fork at the front, with settings specifically tailored to maintain the same riding feel as before.
The hardware at the back is the same as it used to be, only this time it comes with revised spring and damping settings for the horizontal back-link setup, a reduced spring rate, and optimized initial preload. These changes should enhance, first and foremost, cornering stability.
When it comes to the braking system, Japanese engineers opted to install radial-mount four-piston front brake calipers instead of the previous axial-mount two-piston units. On top of that, the ABS calibration has changed.
There is now expanded smartphone connectivity to go with the motorcycle, bringing updated navigation and voice commands, including searching destinations, adding waypoints, and changing route order.
Then, an updated 4.3-inch TFT color instrument panel with two display layouts shows info on things like speed, engine rpm, gear position, and pretty much everything that has to do with the two-wheeler.
There is a visual change as well that is introduced by the refreshed Ninja 650, and that comes as a wider front fender that covers more of the fork outer tubes. Then, the seat position now stands 30.9 inches (780 mm) off the ground, allowing for a relatively upright riding position.
When it comes to the accessories available for the motorcycle, Kawasaki is throwing in, for the first time, the Kawasaki Quick Shifter (KQS) that allows the bike to upshift without the use of the clutch, as long as the engine operates above 2,500 rpm.
Kawasaki says the 2027 Ninja 650 ABS lands on American dealer lots by the end of October, and that it will sell in four color combinations: Lime Green, Galaxy Silver, Metallic Matte Twilight Blue/Candy Persimmon Red, and Metallic Flat Spark Black/Metallic Carbon Gray.
Depending on the color chosen, the motorcycle will set people back $8,099 for standard hues, or $8,299 for the special colors and graphics.

Acura to Launch Three New SUVs in the U.S., Including Its Largest Ever With Eight Seats
15 photos
Photo: Acura
Following a period of trouble one or two years ago, the automotive industry, at least the one over in America, seems to be on a rebound. And there’s no better indication of that than the rising sales in the luxury segment.
Take Japanese Acura , for instance. In the first nine months of the year, the Honda offshoot brags about growing faster than several established luxury competitors that it does not name. Compared to the same period of last year, it sold 4.4 percent more cars.
The growth was driven, in part, by one of its models, the MDX, which not only managed to hold on to the title of best-selling three-row luxury SUV of all time, but also increased its sales by a staggering 25 percent.
On top of that, the carmaker’s ADX and Integra models lead the sales charts in their respective segments, with just three months left in the year.
All of the above seems to have seeded into the heads of the company’s execs the idea that there is more room to grow on the market for Acura. And this week, that idea materialized into a new product plan for the near future.
As you know, at the time of writing, the company sells just four models on the American market, namely the Integra sport sedan and the three SUVs, namely the ADX, RDX, and MDX. These will be joined in the coming years by three more SUVs, including the largest the Japanese have ever made, targeting segments it hasn’t played in so far.
Two of these machines will land in 2028. The first is a new adventure-ready vehicle that will bring a luxury touch to off-roading activities, something more and more people seem to be into these days. No details about it have been released so far.
The second SUV will be the next, fourth generation of the RDX, but we already knew about that. The SUV will, however, become the company’s first product to be fitted with a two-motor hybrid drivetrain.
The star of the announcement is, however, the new eight-passenger SUV that will hit the market later down the line. We’re told this vehicle will become the largest one Acura has ever made, fitting right above the seven-passenger MDX, and will directly target families in need of roomier rides, among others.
On top of the three SUVs, Acura also announced it is working on a new hybrid V6 powertrain, aimed to fit under the hood of the RDX above all. No details about it have been revealed so far, but we expect that to change soon.
We will keep an eye on Acura and its dealings in the U.S. market and report back once we know more about that.

New Zenos E10 Is a 380-HP British Sports Car That Weighs Less Than a Mazda MX-5 Miata
6 photos
Photo: Zenos
Chances are you may not know that much about Zenos Cars , especially its E10 model, unless you live in the United Kingdom, but the British automaker’s model is now back for 2027.
We are talking about a new generation of the Zenos E10, which is the successor to the one made between 2015 and 2016. The original E10 is estimated to have been made in over 100 units, and it is yet unknown how many of the latest will see the light of day, as the company hasn’t announced this detail at the time of writing.
The new 2027 Zenos E10 family is said to “ provide high-performance and advanced engineering at a time when new, pure-bred sports cars are increasingly rare. ” And who are we to contradict them? Especially when it comes to the latter part, because these things are almost unicorns in today’s automotive kingdom.
Zenos’ new E10 sports a carbon fiber tub, an extruded aluminum chassis, and benefits from full carbon fiber bodywork. This means that it is on the very lightweight side of things. In fact, the automaker says that it tips the scales at only 1,742 pounds (790 kg). In order to better understand the weight of the 2027 E10, we will remind you that the aging Mazda MX-5 ND, aka the fourth generation, has a curb weight of 2,183 pounds (990 kg) in its base flavor.
Photo: Zenos But what powers it? A 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine that pushes out 380 brake horsepower (385 ps/283 kW ) at 6,000 rpm and 376 pound-feet (510 Nm) of torque between 3,000 and 4,500 rpm. This applies to the E10 rZ, and it translates to around 480 brake horsepower (487 ps/353 kW) per metric ton (2,205 lbs). That’s pretty much on par with the iconic Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster , more than the Maserati MC20, and roughly the same as the E10 R (old one).
In addition to the rZ version of the new Zenos E10, the company also offers it in the r2 configuration. This model uses a 2.3-liter engine said to deliver 300 hp (304 ps/221 kW) at 6,000 rpm, and 313 pound-feet (425 Nm) of torque at 3,500 rpm. It has a curb weight of 1,742 pounds (790 kg), and it translates to 380 brake horsepower (385 ps/283 kW) per metric ton. That’s roughly similar to the Lamborghini Gallardo LP 570-4 Spyder Performante and the Ferrari 458 Italia .
Zenos says that “ all significant weight ” is “ inboard of both front and rear axles, ” and this includes the engine and gearbox. The new E10 features a fully independent front suspension with pushrod and inboard-mounted dampers for reduced drag. Both engines are turbocharged, have new induction and chargecooler packages, and are connected to a six-speed manual transmission for more driving engagement.
Conventional coil over dampers are found at the rear, mounted to the aluminum subframe that holds the engine and gearbox. There is also a limited-slip differential for enhanced traction at high-speed cornering, and the revised gear linkage mechanism is said to allow for quicker and more precise gear shifts.
Photo: Zenos The new Zenos E10 sports new headlights, as well as new ducting for better cooling of the front brakes, as well as revised radiator packs. The side skirts have also been upgraded for improved aerodynamics. The changes continue on the inside, where a new dashboard panel is on deck, complete with a fresh driver display, and the automaker also mentions the weatherproof switchgear, the new, in-house-made carbon fiber seats offered as standard, and a few other bits and bobs.
The car is offered with a full windscreen and wipers, or a race wind deflector panel. The stopping power is supplied by the uprated brakes, with new larger rotors, hugged by the four-piston calipers and brake pads every time the driver pressed the middle peddle. There is a master cylinder on deck, too, and Zenos says the stopping power and pedal feel have been significantly improved over the old E10.
Interested parties can order the new 2027 Zenos E10 in Midnight Black, Volcano Red, Nitro Blue, Race White, Screaming Green, and Firebust Yellow exterior paint finishes, and they can also opt for a bespoke color for more customization. Both the rZ and the r2 versions rides on 16-inch front and 17-inch rear alloys, shod in 195/50 and 225/45 tires, respectively, and to absolutely no one’s surprise, they are rear-wheel drive.
But how much does the 2027 Zenos E10 cost? In the United Kingdom, you are looking at a minimum of 115,900 GBP for the E10 rZ, according to the company, which translates to $153,420 at today’s exchange rate. Quite surprisingly, the less powerful 2027 E10 r2 is actually more expensive, as pricing in this case kicks off at 129,900 GBP ($171,955).
So, is the new Zenos E10 something you’d consider buying? Let us know your thoughts about this model in the comments area below.

2027 Honda Civic Sedan and Hatchback Arrive in the US, New Sport-L Trim Will Start Below $28,500
7 photos
Photo: Honda
Since we’re deep within the fall season, American Honda is preoccupied with the 2027 model year novelties, and it recently announced the refreshed 2027 Honda Passport TrailSport mid-size SUV is making its way into dealerships now, plus the updated 2027 Honda Civic Type R gaining sharper performance and handling, new comfort features and technologies, and more.
Now it’s time to also see what’s new for the 2027 Honda Civic sedan and hatchback models, which are dubbed by the company as “America’s best-selling compact car” series. Indeed, American Honda posted its best September deliveries this year since 2020 as well as the best Q3 results since 2019.
Honda’s namesake brand surged by almost 18% in September 2026 to almost 112k units, reached over 358k vehicle deliveries during the third quarter of the year, up more than nine percentage points, and also surged almost five percent year-to-date with a total of 1,045,593 sales. During that time, the Civic series has surged by more than five percent to over 195k units over the past nine months.
As such, it’s no wonder that Honda is eager to bring it up to 2027 model year specifications and release it into showrooms as soon as possible. Called “sleek and fun-to-drive,” the 2027 Honda Civic series is arriving at nationwide dealerships now, complete with a new Sport-L trim level ready to join the range by the end of the year.
The 2027 Honda Civic Sedan pricing kicks off at an MSRP of $24,995 sans the $1,295 destination charge. That’s for the LX model, and the Sport begins at $26,995 while the new Sport-L is $28,495, all three featuring the 2.0-liter engine and CVT. The hybrid versions are Sport Hybrid and Sport Touring Hybrid, respectively, starting from $29,695 or $32,695.
Next up, the hatchback model is costlier: there are Sport, Sport-L, Sport Hybrid, and Sport Touring Hybrid versions from $28,195 through $33,895. Slotting between the Civic Sport and Sport Hybrid models, the first-ever Civic Sport-L comes with the leather upholstery from the Sport Touring Hybrid, heated front seats, power-adjustable front seats, dual-zone climate control, a passenger-side seatback pocket, vanity mirrors with illumination, and silver-colored interior trim, all previously exclusive to the hybrid or Sport Touring Hybrid models.
"Civic has earned its place as America's best-selling compact car1 by delivering the fun, efficiency and value that customers expect from Honda," said Luis Guerra, assistant vice president of Honda National Auto Sales at American Honda Motor Co., Inc. "With the new Civic Sport-L, we're making some of Civic's most desirable premium features more accessible, giving buyers another smart reason to choose Civic."
Additionally, the 2027 Civic Sport Touring Hybrid model gets the new Honda S+ Shift technology from the 2026 Honda Prelude, which “simulates a performance transmission for the ultimate electrified Honda driving experience, including virtual rev-matched downshifts and gear holding, plus enhanced engine sounds.”

source_document.body:
The world record for the longest journey on an electric motorcycle on a single charge has just been absolutely demolished.
And it was done so by a Zero Motorcycles rider traveling 436.5 km (271.2 miles) before finally running out of juice.
The ride, completed by Belgian rider Jelle Verstaen aboard a Zero DS electric motorcycle, earned a new Guinness World Records title and blew past the previous record of 310.7 km (193 miles) by more than 125 km (78 miles).
And this wasn’t some one-off aerodynamic streamliner built specifically to chase a record. The bike was a production Zero DS equipped with the company’s optional Power Tank, bringing total battery capacity to 19.2 kWh. Verstaen was joined for the ride by two others on Zeros as well, with all three beating the previous record.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The record attempt began high in the French Alps and eventually wound its way down toward the Mediterranean coast, with Verstaen aiming to maintain an average cruising speed of around 52 km/h (32 mph).
That might not sound particularly fast for a motorcycle – and it certainly wasn’t – but speed was very much the enemy here. Aerodynamic drag increases dramatically as speeds rise, making relatively slow riding one of the best ways to stretch an electric motorcycle’s battery.
The result was a ride that lasted deep into the night and through the next morning.
Zero says the team specifically chose nighttime riding to reduce traffic, helping Verstaen maintain a steady, efficient pace. That became especially important as the route transitioned from the Alps toward lower elevations and eventually the Mediterranean.
And while Verstaen ultimately took the crown, he of course wasn’t the only Zero rider out there seeing just how far an electric motorcycle could go.
His riding partners on a Zero SR/S managed 350 km (217 miles) on a charge, while a DSR/X stretched its battery to 384 km (239 miles). Both would make for impressive range figures on their own, but the DS simply kept going.
The final portion of the record ride apparently wasn’t exactly pleasant, either.
Heavy rain arrived for roughly the last 100 km (62 miles), turning what was already an overnight endurance run into an increasingly soggy battle toward the finish.
But Verstaen and the DS continued onward until the bike ultimately covered 436.5 km, surpassing the previous record by more than 40%.
The ride was tracked using GPS and independently witnessed as part of the Guinness World Records verification process.
For an electric motorcycle carrying less than 20 kWh of battery, traveling 271 miles on a charge is an impressive demonstration of just how efficient two-wheeled EVs can become when ridden carefully.
Electrek’s Take
This is quite a feat, and I love seeing electric motorcycles used for all kinds of challenges . There’s still a surprisingly persistent belief that electric motorcycles are inherently short-range machines, and traveling over 270 miles on less than 20 kWh of battery is a pretty good way to demonstrate just how much energy a motorcycle actually needs to move a person down the road.
But there are also some fairly large asterisks here.
For one thing, the route started high in the French Alps and worked its way toward the Mediterranean, meaning the riders enjoyed a significant net decrease in elevation. It wasn’t exactly 271 miles of coasting downhill, of course, and there were plenty of climbs and other terrain along the way, but gravity was nevertheless lending a helping hand over the course of the trip.
The bigger factor, though, was speed.
A target of around 52 km/h (32 mph) is incredibly efficient for an electric motorcycle, but it’s not representative of how most people actually ride motorcycles on the open road. At typical highway speeds, aerodynamic drag would chew through that battery much more quickly.
In fact, that low target speed may also help explain why so much of the attempt took place overnight. Maintaining around 32 mph on roads where daytime traffic is moving considerably faster could range from annoying to downright dangerous. Doing it in the middle of the night with much lighter traffic makes considerably more sense.
So no, this doesn’t mean you should expect to hop on a Zero DS and ride 271 miles at 70 mph without stopping.
But that’s not really the point of a record attempt, either.
Records are about finding the limits of what a machine can do under carefully optimized conditions, and Zero just demonstrated that a production electric motorcycle carrying less energy than many plug-in hybrid cars can travel more than 270 miles through the real world on a single charge.
That’s a heck of an achievement – even if you probably don’t want to replicate the pace on your next road trip.

All-New Mercedes AMG GT SUV Gets Rid of the Camouflage Ahead of the Impending Presentation - in CGI
28 photos
Photo: marianvalentincilibeanu / Instagram
The Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, the Ferrari Luce, or the Jaguar Type 01 – what do these models all have in common ? Quite a few things, actually…
All three of them are novel ultra-luxury and high-performance ‘sedan’ models with four doors. All three of them have more than 1,000 horsepower in their top configurations. All three of them have some naturally controversial design languages, both outside and inside. And, of course, all three of them are fully electric vehicles featuring new 800- or 850-volt dedicated architectures intended to remain relevant into the next decade.
Of course, all three of them have elicited very strong feelings across the Internet, with both specialists and amateurs discussing their new design languages. Funny enough, while all three of them are incredibly controversial, they’re also wildly different, showing that stylists now strive more than ever to stand out in any crowd, even though it may be the wrong one.
Anyway, there’s also one major detail that sets them apart: only one of them is going to receive a high-riding sibling before the end of the year. That’s going to be the Mercedes- AMG GT model, of course, which is getting the SUV option on October 17 at home in Stuttgart, with the Mercedes-AMG crossover built from scratch ready to anchor the fresh AMG.EA platform and showcase the direction of the brand’s future performance strategy.
There have been numerous reports, rumors, spied prototypes, and renderings – the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators are keeping very close to this one instead of dwelling aimlessly across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
Now, here’s also Marian Valentin Cilibeanu, aka 'Cili' (known as marianvalentincilibeanu on social media), a Romanian virtual artist who also envisions the next Mercedes-AMG GT model in SUV form in a bid to get rid of the funky camouflage of the prototypes. Mercedes-AMG's first ground-up electric GT SUV model engineered entirely in-house might arrive at dealerships in early 2027, so it’s no wonder that everyone’s in a hurry to see it, by the way.
Mercedes-AMG’s first independently developed SUV, in these renderings, looks a bit less controversial than the GT 4-Door Coupe because now there are more vertical surfaces to play with, and the pixel master also deploys a trick – he mixes the larger three-pointed LED star daytime running lights with a full-width LED bar as if they’re a continuous element.
The front also has the new EV AMG grille on full display, now raised in a more elevated position compared to the GT 4-Door to allow new design elements to form the more classic front bumper. There’s just one CGI shot of the SUV going on a winding road, so we only catch a glimpse of the profile, and there’s no rear, but it’s pretty clear the AMG GT SUV will strive to remain practical as it prepares to fight the likes of the Bentley Torcal but also the Porsche Cayenne Electric, among other rivals. source_document.body:
Johnson & Johnson beat analyst expectations in the third quarter but left Wall Street wanting more; BMS dominated the news cycle on Monday with a Phase 3 win validating its $4.1 billion RayzeBio buy and mixed data in a late-stage pulmonary fibrosis trial; Revolution Medicines’ newly approved pancreatic cancer drug works better for patients with certain mutations; and Caribou Biosciences may be on its way out.

> Listen on Amazon Music
> Listen on iHeart
> Watch on YouTube
Third quarter earnings are upon us, as Johnson & Johnson kicked off this spooky season on Tuesday with a report “in line” with analyst expectations. While the earnings beat was supported by the company’s innovative medicines division, J&J’s stock slipped about 4% on the underperformance of its medtech unit.
Meanwhile, Bristol Myers Squibb, which reports Q3 earnings Oct. 29, has had a “mixed” week. The company’s lung disease asset scored a low-dose win in a Phase 3 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis trial but failed to significantly improve exhalation capacity at a higher dose. BMS enjoyed a more decisive Phase 3 victory with RYZ-101 as the asset, picked up in the company’s $4.1 billion acquisition of RayzeBio, improved progression-free survival for patients with a rare type of gastrointestinal tract cancer. This all comes as BMO Capital Markets questions the company’s plan to manage the upcoming loss of exclusivity for Opdivo and Eliquis.
One company analysts will be watching closely when smaller biotechs begin to report Q3 earnings is Revolution Medicines, whose “miracle” pancreatic cancer drug Rasonque won FDA approval in August. While the drug’s launch is widely expected to set records, RevMed dipped last week after the FDA released review documents showing that Rasonque appeared to work better in some patient subgroups than others.
Speaking of smaller biotechs, it’s been a rough month for Adecto Pharmaceuticals and Aviceda Therapeutics, both of which are exiting the scene . And last week, news broke that Caribou Biosciences —co-founded by Nobel Prize-winning CRISPR pioneer Jennifer Doudna—has discontinued its entire clinical-stage pipeline and will part with 87 employees—the majority of its staff—by the end of the year.
Finally, enjoy our thoughts on the Major League Baseball playoffs and our favorite all-time Halloween movies.
